dct_description_sm: For the present work, we aim to re-analyse the Nunavik Child Development Study (NCDS) data in order to better understand Selenium (Se) neurotoxicity and Se effects on Methylmercury (MeHg) neurotoxicity in children at 5 and 11 years old, and estimate dietary sources of Se intake among 11 year-old children in Nunavik.  More specifically, we aim to: 1. Study the association between prenatal and current Se status (5- and 11-yr blood) and neurobehavioral outcomes (cognitive, behavioral, visual, motor) in children at 5 and 11 years of age, and establish (if any) the threshold of Se neurotoxicity among children with high Se status. higher Se status to maintain optimal selenoproteins' activity. 2. Study how prenatal MeHg neurodevelopmental toxicity (cognitive, behavioral, visual, motor) in children at 5 and 11 years of age is mitigated by prenatal and current Se status; 3. Estimate dietary sources of Se intake among 11-year old children.

dct_title_s: Is high Se intake from marine diet during pregnancy and childhood neurotoxic or mitigating the adverse effects of MeHg exposure on child development?
